Don't launch LC.AppHost or LC.Api directly from an agent worktree. A developer instance may already own the Aspire dashboard or service ports, and detached startup failures can surface as Windows crash dialogs. Use `python tools/test.py --suite light --stack backend` for backend verification. For a full-stack run, the only sanctioned route is `node tools/control-lc/control-lc.mjs launch`: it gives this worktree its own stack on free ports, and `node tools/control-lc/control-lc.mjs cleanup` removes it (see skills/engineering/verify-lc/SKILL.md and dydo/guides/running-lc.md).

Don't start LC.AppHost or LC.Api as a detached process from an agent worktree. Detached hosts outlive the test command, collide with developer ports, and can surface failures as Windows crash dialogs. Use `python tools/test.py --suite light --stack backend` for backend verification. For a full-stack run, the only sanctioned route is `node tools/control-lc/control-lc.mjs launch`: it gives this worktree its own stack on free ports, and `node tools/control-lc/control-lc.mjs cleanup` removes it (see skills/engineering/verify-lc/SKILL.md and dydo/guides/running-lc.md).

Use the one test command instead: python tools/test.py --feature <id> (--heavy adds its Heavy tests), or python tools/test.py --suite light --stack backend.
It runs dotnet test through the suite manifest and queues Heavy runs on the machine-wide lock.

Use the isolated test runner instead: python tools/coverage/run_tests.py --stack=frontend
This avoids cross-process collisions on vitest's istanbul .tmp/ shard staging dir (issue #40).

Use the wrapper instead: python tools/migrations/run_migrations.py $1
It invokes `dotnet ef` with the right paths and updates the hash manifest the drift test checks.

Use pnpm, not npm — frontend migrated per Decision 030. Try: pnpm $1
See dydo/project/decisions/030-frontend-package-manager-pnpm.md
